message.content:
Search this repository very thoroughly for the frontend authentication interceptor that attaches tokens to API requests. I need:

1. The file path of the auth interceptor (likely an Axios interceptor or fetch wrapper that adds Authorization headers or manages tokens)
2. What kinds of tokens it manages (access token, refresh token, etc.)
3. The backend package that validates these tokens

Search for:
- "interceptor" in TypeScript/JavaScript files
- "Authorization" header setting
- "axios.interceptors" or similar patterns
- "accessToken", "refreshToken" patterns
- Files related to API client setup or HTTP client configuration
- Backend JWT or token validation packages

Look in directories like packages/, apps/, src/, etc. Be very thorough - check multiple naming conventions.

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

96	func GenerateAccessToken(username string, userID int32, expirationTime time.Time, secret []byte) (string, error) {

100	// generateToken generates a JWT token with the given claims.
101	//
102	// Token structure:
103	// Header: {"alg": "HS256", "kid": "v1", "typ": "JWT"}
104	// Claims: {"name": username, "iss": "memos", "aud": [audience], "sub": userID, "iat": now, "exp": expiry}
105	// Signature: HMACSHA256(base64UrlEncode(header) + "." + base64UrlEncode(payload), secret).
106	func generateToken(username string, userID int32, audience string, expirationTime time.Time, secret []byte) (string, error) {
107		registeredClaims := jwt.RegisteredClaims{
108			Issuer:   Issuer,
109			Audience: jwt.ClaimStrings{audience},
110			IssuedAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now()),
111			Subject:  fmt.Sprint(userID),
112		}
113		if !expirationTime.IsZero() {
114			registeredClaims.ExpiresAt = jwt.NewNumericDate(expirationTime)
115		}
116	
117		// Declare the token with the HS256 algorithm used for signing, and the claims.
118		token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, &ClaimsMessage{
119			Name:             username,
120			RegisteredClaims: registeredClaims,
121		})
122		token.Header["kid"] = KeyID
123	
124		// Create the JWT string.
125		tokenString, err := token.SignedString(secret)
126		if err != nil {
127			return "", err
128		}
129	
130		return tokenString, nil
131	}

9	// ContextKey is the key type for context values.
10	// Using a custom type prevents collisions with other packages.
11	type ContextKey int
12	
13	const (
14		// UserIDContextKey stores the authenticated user's ID.
15		// Set for all authenticated requests.
16		// Use GetUserID(ctx) to retrieve this value.
17		UserIDContextKey ContextKey = iota
18	
19		// AccessTokenContextKey stores the JWT token for token-based auth.
20		// Only set when authenticated via Bearer token.
21		AccessTokenContextKey
22	
23		// UserClaimsContextKey stores the claims from access token.
24		UserClaimsContextKey
25	
26		// RefreshTokenIDContextKey stores the refresh token ID.
27		RefreshTokenIDContextKey
28	)
29	
30	// GetUserID retrieves the authenticated user's ID from the context.
31	// Returns 0 if no user ID is set (unauthenticated request).
32	func GetUserID(ctx context.Context) int32 {
33		if v, ok := ctx.Value(UserIDContextKey).(int32); ok {
34			return v
35		}
36		return 0
37	}
38	
39	// GetAccessToken retrieves the JWT access token from the context.
40	// Returns empty string if not authenticated via bearer token.
41	func GetAccessToken(ctx context.Context) string {
42		if v, ok := ctx.Value(AccessTokenContextKey).(string); ok {
43			return v
44		}
45		return ""
46	}
47	
48	// SetUserInContext sets the authenticated user's information in the context.
49	// This is a simpler alternative to AuthorizeAndSetContext for cases where
50	// authorization is handled separately (e.g., HTTP middleware).
51	//
52	// Parameters:
53	//   - user: The authenticated user
54	//   - accessToken: Set if authenticated via JWT token (empty string otherwise)
55	func SetUserInContext(ctx context.Context, user *store.User, accessToken string) context.Context {
56		ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, UserIDContextKey, user.ID)
57		if accessToken != "" {
58			ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, AccessTokenContextKey, accessToken)
59		}
60		return ctx
61	}

63	// UserClaims represents authenticated user info from access token.
64	type UserClaims struct {
65		UserID   int32
66		Username string
67		Role     string
68		Status   string
69	}

72	// Returns nil if not authenticated via access token.

78	}

Now I have a complete picture. Here is the full report.

---

## Findings

### 1. Frontend Auth Interceptor

**File:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/connect.ts`

This file contains the authentication interceptor. It is **not** an Axios interceptor -- this project uses **ConnectRPC** (`@connectrpc/connect` and `@connectrpc/connect-web`) instead of Axios or a plain fetch wrapper. The interceptor is defined at line 156:

```ts
const authInterceptor: Interceptor = (next) => async (req) => {
```

It is wired into the ConnectRPC transport at line 188:

```ts
const transport = createConnectTransport({
  baseUrl: window.location.origin,
  useBinaryFormat: true,
  fetch: fetchWithCredentials,
  interceptors: [authInterceptor],
});
```

**How it works:**
1. Before every RPC call, it calls `getRequestToken()` to obtain the current access token.
2. It sets the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <token>` (line 99).
3. If the RPC returns a `Code.Unauthenticated` error and this is not already a retry, it attempts to refresh the token via `refreshAccessToken()`, then retries the request once (with an `X-Retry` header to prevent infinite loops).
4. If the refresh also fails, it calls `redirectOnAuthFailure()` (from `/bench/home/work/web/src/utils/auth-redirect.ts`) which clears the stored token and redirects to the auth page.

A separate transport **without** the auth interceptor (line 65-70) is used solely for the refresh-token RPC itself, to prevent recursion.

### 2. Token Types Managed

**Supporting file:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/auth-state.ts`

The frontend manages the following tokens:

- **Access Token (short-lived, 15 minutes):** Stored in both an in-memory variable and `localStorage` (key: `memos_access_token`). Its expiry is stored under `memos_token_expires_at`. This is the token sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every API call.

- **Refresh Token (long-lived, 30 days):** Sent/received as an **HTTP-only cookie** named `memos_refresh`. The frontend never reads or stores this token directly in JavaScript; it is handled by the browser via `credentials: "include"` on fetch calls. The refresh RPC (`refreshAuthClient.refreshToken({})`) sends this cookie automatically and receives a new access token in the response.

- **Token synchronization across tabs:** A `BroadcastChannel` named `memos_token_sync` is used so that when one tab refreshes the access token, all other tabs adopt the new token immediately without making their own refresh requests.

- **Proactive token refresh:** The hook at `/bench/home/work/web/src/hooks/useTokenRefreshOnFocus.ts` refreshes the access token when the user returns to a tab and the token is expired or expiring within 2 minutes (`FOCUS_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_MS`). Normal API request preflight uses a 30-second buffer (`REQUEST_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_MS`).

- **Token expiry buffers** (defined in `auth-state.ts`):
  - `REQUEST_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_MS = 30_000` (30 seconds before expiry, proactively refresh before an API call)
  - `FOCUS_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_MS = 120_000` (2 minutes before expiry, proactively refresh on tab focus)

### 3. Backend Token Validation

**Package:** `/bench/home/work/server/auth/` (Go package `auth`)

**JWT library:** `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5` (v5.3.1, declared in `/bench/home/work/go.mod`)

Key backend files:

- **`/bench/home/work/server/auth/token.go`** -- Token generation and parsing:
  - `GenerateAccessTokenV2()` creates short-lived (15-minute) JWT access tokens signed with HMAC-SHA256 (`HS256`), key ID `v1`, issuer `memos`, audience `user.access-token`. Claims include user ID, username, role, and status.
  - `GenerateRefreshToken()` creates long-lived (30-day) JWT refresh tokens with audience `user.refresh-token` and a `TokenID` for database-based revocation.
  - `GeneratePersonalAccessToken()` / `HashPersonalAccessToken()` create and hash PATs (prefixed `memos_pat_`).
  - `ParseAccessTokenV2()` validates access tokens statelessly (signature + issuer + audience + type claim).
  - `ParseRefreshToken()` validates refresh tokens (signature + issuer + audience + type claim).

- **`/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go`** -- Central authentication logic:
  - `AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2()` -- stateless validation of access tokens (no DB query).
  - `AuthenticateByRefreshToken()` -- validates refresh token signature, then checks the database for revocation and expiry.
  - `AuthenticateByPAT()` -- validates PATs by looking up their SHA-256 hash in the database.
  - `Authenticate()` -- resolves a Bearer token (access token or PAT) into an `AuthResult`.
  - `AuthenticateToUser()` -- tries the Authorization header first, falls back to the refresh token cookie.

- **`/bench/home/work/server/auth/extract.go`** -- Extracts the Bearer token from the `Authorization` header and the refresh token from the `Cookie` header.

- **`/bench/home/work/server/auth/context.go`** -- Stores authenticated user info (user ID, claims, access token) in the Go request context.

- **`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`** -- The backend-side **Connect RPC `AuthInterceptor`** (line 208) that reads the `Authorization` header from every incoming request, delegates to the `Authorizer`/`Authenticator`, and either injects the authenticated identity into the context or returns `CodeUnauthenticated`.

### Summary Table

| Concern | Location | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend interceptor | `/bench/home/work/web/src/connect.ts` | ConnectRPC `Interceptor` adding `Authorization: Bearer` header |
| Access token state | `/bench/home/work/web/src/auth-state.ts` | In-memory + localStorage, 15-min lifetime, BroadcastChannel sync |
| Token refresh on focus | `/bench/home/work/web/src/hooks/useTokenRefreshOnFocus.ts` | Proactive refresh when tab becomes visible |
| Auth failure redirect | `/bench/home/work/web/src/utils/auth-redirect.ts` | Clears token, redirects to `/auth` |
| Query client retry | `/bench/home/work/web/src/lib/query-client.ts` | Skips React Query retry on `Unauthenticated` (interceptor already handled it) |
| Backend token pkg | `/bench/home/work/server/auth/token.go` | `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5`, HMAC-SHA256, access + refresh + PAT generation/parsing |
| Backend authenticator | `/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go` | Stateless access token validation, DB-checked refresh tokens, PAT hash lookup |
| Backend interceptor | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go` | Server-side Connect RPC `AuthInterceptor` |
